newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's sugar imports up 7.3 pct to 0.5 mln/1996.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's sugar imports up 7.3 pct to 0.5 mln/1996.

text.p: Morocco's raw sugar imports, mainly from South America, rose 7.3 percent to half a million tonnes in 1996 compared with the previous year, the Office des Changes regulatory bureau said.
In a monthly newsletter received on Friday, the state-run office said: "Morocco raw sugar imports rose to 0.51 million tonnes in 1996 from 0.47 million in 1995."
Sugar purchase period was calculated on the calendar basis from January to December, the office said.
Raw sugar imports in value remained nearly stable at 1.348 billion dirhams ($145 million) in 1996 compared with 1.319 billion dirhams in 1995, it said.

Nearly half of the country's sugar imports were made by Cosumar refinery, a subsidiary of Morocco's largest private conglomerate ONA Group, since the authorities gradually liberalised the commodity market in May 1996, a Moroccan market analyst said.
The Casablanca-based Cosumar which refines an average 2,000 tonnes of raw sugar per day, remains the main sugar importer and refiner, the analyst said.

"Cosumar's activity registered a relative stagnation, which had an impact on its consolidated turnover...It only rose by 0.8 percent to 3.14 billion dirhams in 1996 compared with the previous year," he said.
But it posted a positive net profit of 223.6 million dirhams ($23.6 million) in 1996, up 43.6 percent from 155.7 million dirhams in 1995, he added.

Cosumar, which recently appointed Lekbir Belaidi as new managing director, is expected to inaugurate a new sugar refinery unit in June "to replace its old Casablanca refining installations, increase its production capacity and improve the quality of its sugar products," he said.
The new unit cost was estimated at around 100 million dirhams ($10.7 million), the analyst added.
Brazil and other South America sugar producers remain Morocco's main providers, a trade ministry official said.
According to commodity traders, Morocco's sugar imports are expected to stagnate around 500,000 tonnes in 1997 due to domestic sluggish consumption.
Cosumar officials were not immediately available for comment.
